title: Private deployments cost allocator & scenario playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for modeling Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and simple ROI scenarios for Private deployments (on-prem + cloud VPC) and for producing concrete licensing + support bundle recommendations. The goal is to provide product, sales engineering, and solutions teams with a repeatable, componentized allocator that can be adapted to customer inputs.

Assumptions and modeling approach (high level)
- Componentized model: break costs into discrete buckets so we can recombine: HW (capex), datacenter costs (space/power/cooling), network egress & WAN, software license, support & SLA premium, ops headcount, amortization schedule, cloud VPC infra (compute + storage + networking), and optional professional services.
- Time horizon: 3-year baseline (can extend to 5y for enterprise CAPEX-heavy deals).
- Amortization: CapEx amortized straight-line across chosen term (default 3 years) with an option to model accelerated depreciation for tax-sensitive customers.
- Currency: USD. Quick sensitivity knobs: discount rate, utilization %, peak:average ratio, and reserved vs on-demand pricing for VPC compute.

Scenario definitions (componentized)
- Scenario A: On-prem owned (customer buys HW, Redwood licenses + Gold support)
  - HW purchase (rack GPUs, NVMe, nodes) amortized 3y
  - Data center colocation: $/rackU monthly incl cooling, power kWh & PUE factor
  - Network: L3 transit + cross-connect fees
  - Software: Redwood private-license (per-instance or per-GPU) and support bundle (Standard/Gold/Enterprise)
  - Ops: site reliability + infra engineer FTEs allocated as percent of time to inference stack

- Scenario B: VPC private (customer uses cloud VPC deployment managed by Redwood)
  - Cloud compute: reserved instances/savings plans vs on-demand vs spot for batch workloads
  - Storage: block and object storage costs for model artifacts, KV cache, and checkpoints
  - Networking: VPC egress, VPN/DirectConnect cost, inter-AZ traffic
  - Software: Redwood license fee (lower capex-like fee, higher per-unit runtime usage) + optional support SLA
  - Management: fewer on-site ops FTEs, but more cloud-networking and security FTE effort

- Scenario C: Hybrid (on-prem baseline + cloud burst for peaks)
  - Core latency-sensitive serving on-prem, batch/overflow on cloud
  - Mix ratio configurable: e.g., 80/20 steady-state vs peak-offload
  - Dual licensing discount if customer signs both on-prem + cloud commitments

Key cost buckets and example variables to capture (text-form spreadsheet columns)
- Hardware_capex_per_node: sample value placeholder (e.g., $120k per 8xA100 node)
- Nodes_required: derived from QPS and model FLOPS/throughput profile
- Amortization_years: default 3
- Colocation_monthly_per_rack: regional inputs required
- Power_kWh_per_node: use nameplate + PUE factor to estimate monthly power cost
- Cloud_compute_hourly: cloud SKU list and mapping to equivalent throughput (use benchmarked tokens/sec)
- Reserved_commit_discount: % (0-70%)
- License_flat_fee: per-instance/year or per-GPU/year choices
- License_runtime_fee: per-inference / per-token alternative pricing column
- Support_tier_multiplier: Standard=1.0, Gold=1.25, Enterprise=1.6 (example multipliers)
- Ops_FTE_cost_per_year: fully-burdened

Quick worked example (narrative, not full numbers)
- Customer X needs 200 QPS steady for a 2-token avg response and heavy KV cache. Benchmarking suggests one 8-GPU node can handle ~20 QPS for this model. Nodes_required = ceil(200/20) = 10 nodes.
- On-prem: 10 nodes * HW_capex_per_node ($120k) = $1.2M capex. Amortized over 3y => $400k/year. Add colocation + power ~$8k/mo/rack + ops FTE 0.5 of one engineer ($120k/year * 0.5 = $60k/year) + license/support $200k/year => blended TCOYr1 ~ $400k + $96k + $60k + $200k = ~$756k/yr (illustrative).
- VPC: Equivalent throughput requires N cloud instances, but with reserved upfront commit we model 40% lower compute cost vs on-demand. Total VPC run cost calculated as compute + storage + networking + Redwood runtime license (runtime fee model) => blended ~ $820k/yr (if low reserved commitment), but if customer does a 1-year committed reserved plan (60% discount) cloud cost drops to $520k/yr.
- Hybrid: Core 6 nodes on-prem + burst 4 nodes on cloud during peak windows => combine amortized on-prem cost + variable cloud cost. Hybrid frequently yields best SLA+cost mix for customers with spiky workloads.

Optimization levers & recommendations for sell-throughs
1) Licensing shape: offer two paths
  - CapEx-friendly bundle: lower runtime fees, higher upfront license for on-prem (good for customers with capex budget and 3y+ horizon).
  - OpEx-friendly bundle: lower upfront, higher per-runtime usage for VPC customers.
2) Support bundling tiers
  - Standard: basic incident support, 9x5, ticketed
  - Gold: 24x7 escalation, 1-hr P1 SLA, included runbooks and quarterly onsite or remote health checks
  - Enterprise: dedicated TAM, capacity reservations, custom fallback model variants, and legal SLAs
  Pricing guidance: treat support as multiplier on base license; also offer credits for multi-year commitments.
3) Infrastructure allocation optimizer (how to recommend capacity mix)
  - Input knobs: steady_qps, peak_qps, peak_duration_hours_per_week, acceptable_latency_percentile, budget_target
  - Policy: put baseline 60-85% of steady state on-prem if on-prem is available; place remaining headroom to VPC bursts. If budget_target strict -> increase cloud reserved commit to reduce runtime hourly.
4) Cost engineering levers
  - Quantization + mixed precision to reduce GPU type and lower HW_capex_per_node
  - KV cache sizing and local cache hit rate tuning to reduce tokens generated and cloud egress
  - Batching windows for non-latency-sensitive requests (multi-tenant batching across customers in dedicated deployments)
  - Autoscaling cooldown and predictive spiky scheduling to minimize cloud spot churn

Sales packaging and discounting playbook (practical templates)
- Template A: On-prem 3y bundle
  - 3y HW purchase + Redwood Private license (one-time + annual support) + 20% professional services setup fee
  - Discount schedule: 10% off license for 3y prepay, 25% off support if they commit to enterprise SLA for 3y
- Template B: VPC subscription
  - Minimum 12-month committed spend for reserved capacity (target 50% of peak run hours reserved)
  - Lower setup fee, higher per-runtime fee; include a free migration week and 2 health checks in year 1
- Template C: Hybrid commitment
  - Dual-contract discount: if customer commits to both on-prem license and 12mo reserved VPC, apply 15% cross-product discount + included traffic peering credits

Break-even thought experiment (how to spot when on-prem wins)
- On-prem becomes better when: 3y amortized capex + ops + support annualized < cloud committed cost for equivalent throughput AND customer wants long-term predictable unit cost. Watch for utilization > 65% steady-state and low seasonal peaks.
- Cloud wins when: demand highly variable with low baseline & big peaks, or when the customer cannot/will not invest capex and values operational simplicity.

Data collection checklist for rapid quoting (what SEs should gather before running allocator)
- Target QPS and p95 latency requirement
- Typical prompt length distribution and average response tokens
- Peak (% of baseline) and peak hours/week
- Security/compliance constraints (requires air-gapped or can use VPC)
- Existing data center footprint and colocation contracts (rackU available, contract length, kWh rates)
- Preferred procurement model (capex vs opex)
- Budget cycle timing (fiscal quarter / year)

Open questions and follow-ups
- Need to confirm standard multipliers for support tiers with finance (to replace illustrative multipliers). Jira PD-4387 tracks this.
- Benchmark mapping: produce a 1:1 mapping from our public benchmark tokens/sec for each model to cloud SKUs and to on-prem node types (action: bench-team to produce artifacts, GH link above).
- Tax and depreciation nuances per region (finance to advise on accelerated schedules)

Next steps (short list)
- Finalize parameter defaults (ops FTE burden, colocation regional baselines) — owner: Samir — due 2026-02-28
- Produce a lightweight spreadsheet generator from the allocator template (GH: private-deployments/tco-scripts) — owner: Jordan — due 2026-03-10
- Run 4 pilot customer quotes and capture real contract numbers to refine multipliers — owner: Ava — ongoing (target complete Q2 2026)

Notes to self (scratchpad items)
- Consider adding a simple visual decision tree for SEs: low budget + low steady -> cloud; high steady utilization -> on-prem; spiky -> hybrid.
- Include a short FAQ for procurement teams explaining difference between license upfront vs runtime billing (help shorten procurement cycles).

End of playbook (working doc)
